subject: Multiple-session to estimate SE and lower and upper confidence interval of D for a site without detections

messages.author: a8324acf47515438
messages.subject: Multiple-session to estimate SE and lower and upper confidence interval of D for a site without detections
parts:
Hi Murray,

We recently conducted a session without a single detection. I would like to know, given the sampling effort, how confident I can be that not as single individual was present in the study site during the survey :-)

Based on the suggestion of Jose Jimenez on Researchgate, I started to run multisession secr analysis including one session that does not contain a single detection. The idea is to use the information from the site without any detection (sites and usage), and the capture histories from the other sites with positives results to compute the SE and lower and upper confidence interval of the density estimate for the site without detections. I plan to use sessions with positive results conducted in similar habitats and with similar topographical features, as habitat and topographical features could affect detection probability.

So far I used session as session factor on Density and run following model: M0 <-secr.fit(capthist_NWA_VSN, mask=list(mask_13_NWA,mask_13_VSN), model = list(D~session, g0~1, sigma~1),verify=TRUE)

Does it make sense and if yes, how many sessions with positive results would be needed to get a good approximation of SE and lower and upper confidence interval for the site without a single detection?

I noticed that sometimes the variance calculation failed.

Many thanks in advance

Best wishes

Fridolin

messages.author: b1d2e118c1689e57
messages.subject: RE: Multiple-session to estimate SE and lower and upper confidence interval of D for a site without detections
parts:
Hi Fridolin,

 

I’ve run a (basic) analysis like this before to estimate density where individuals were reasonably expected to exist but none were captured. As you propose, it calculates a (low) density with standard error https://www.doc.govt.nz/globalassets/documents/science-and-technical/drds352entire.pdf

 

If you are in the converse situation, where you want to reasonably confirm expected absence, you would also need to set some reasonable subjective expectation of what constitutes absence, as SECR will always give some positive (but small) value of density for the upper bound, if not also point, estimate.

 

Based on SECR we implement a framework for this called Rapid Eradication Assessment, which is used to confirm the absence of pests on islands following eradication and a series of non-detections. The original methods paper is here: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/1365-2664.12147 and further simulations here: https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/1365-2664.12753 and we have a forthcoming paper in review with further extensions which are implemented in a beta form here: www.rea.is (i.e. still a bit buggy).

 

I am happy to provide R code. There is still always more work to do developing the REA method. In particular the underlying population growth model is simplistic (unbounded exponential) and so the REA is only really suitable when you are expecting to detect <10 individuals if any (recall you are really expecting none). We’re currently working on a different tool to estimate number of pest management survivors when >0 but still low (and unmarked cues).

 

Regards,

   James

messages.author: 78ef92d8ca24b10c
messages.subject: Re: Multiple-session to estimate SE and lower and upper confidence interval of D for a site without detections
parts:
Just my $0.02 :

If there are no detections at one site (and on the other grids, the populations are relatively detectable), I would imagine the gradient for the likelihood of log(D_sessionwithoutdetections) looks pretty flat: the likelihood for log(D) = -15 vs. -20, vs. -30 might be nearly exactly the same.You might be able to get a usable derived estimate of D if you fit the multi-session model using  the conditional likelihood? Could also use MCMC (which I believe Jose Jimenez is suggests on researchgate), which might provide a little more flexibility for modeling variation in the detection parameters (e.g., g0/sigma as random effects) and might better describe the uncertainty around the realized population size/density in this particular problematic region, albeit more slowly. 

John

messages.author: 78ef92d8ca24b10c
messages.subject: Re: Multiple-session to estimate SE and lower and upper confidence interval of D for a site without detections
parts: Or maybe realized N for some subset of the mask around the problematic grid (sufficiently well buffered) works well enough? I think you would have to get around the variance estimation failures (eg, treat each session as different realizations of the same homogeneous or inhomogenous—covariate driven or session trend—point process). I guess it depends upon what else you are trying to do.

Thank you John,

Yes, you are right Jose Jimenez suggested to use a Bayesian approach but with exception of SPACECAP this is new land for me. So I prefer to use secr for the moment. I will check if it works better if I use a conditional likelihood. I already got some results using the likelihood. To get an estimation of the realized N, I need anyway to fit a model using the secr.fit function. I planned to use region.N at the end to get an estimation of the number of individuals present in each of the sites. If N<1 I would conclude that no individual is present at this particular site.

I will also try oSCR

Best wishes

Fridolin
